title: Declare the complete physical bevel-edge set before assigning weights
problem: A mesh can be closed, all-quad, and technically clean while omitted weighted edge segments create bumps, pinches, and broken highlight rails after Bevel and Subdivision. If intended edges are inferred from the final weight map, the omissions are impossible to audit.
preconditions: the reference or design decision establishes which transitions require a real physical radius
persistent edge IDs are available before declaration and assignment
the Bevel modifier uses WEIGHT limiting and remains live before Subdivision Surface
Smooth by Angle is recorded for the remaining interpolation policy
required_observations: the explicitly declared persistent edge-ID set
the independently measured nonzero bevel-weight edge-ID set
base-cage connectivity, quads, manifoldness, and modifier order
fixed-view MatCap or grazing-light continuity around the entire declared transition
action_policy: Declare the complete semantic physical-radius edge set before assigning any weights; do not derive design intent from the resulting weight map.
Assign weight through a separate typed decision, then compare actual weighted IDs with the declaration exactly.
Inspect the full transition around the object, including sides and corners that may be hidden in the primary view.
Keep Bevel before Subdivision Surface for this tested physical-rim workflow and leave both modifiers unapplied.
Treat a clean manifold/all-quad result as necessary technical evidence, not proof that sharp-edge coverage is complete.
If the sets differ, return to the missing persistent IDs and repair the assignment before judging normal policy or adding topology.
expected_effects: the semantic audit reports no missing or unexpected weighted edge IDs
continuous rim width and highlight flow survive Bevel-before-SubD evaluation
an omitted edge remains diagnosable even when the evaluated mesh is closed and all-quad
authored intent survives saving and fresh-process inspection
failure_predicates: intent source is WEIGHT_ASSIGNMENT_INFERRED when completeness must be proven
declared and weighted persistent edge-ID sets differ
local protrusions, pinches, or highlight discontinuities align with missing weight segments
the audit passes only because omitted edges disappeared from both intent and assignment records
recovery: restore the explicit declaration and assign every missing edge ID in a scoped transaction
remove any unexpected weighted IDs that do not represent a physical design radius
repeat the full-perimeter MatCap check with the live modifier stack
revisit reference-defined sharp intent rather than mechanically weighting every mesh edge

sources.description: Crown and saddle all-quad panels compare complete and eight-edge-omission maps through typed declaration, assignment, and Smooth-by-Angle decisions.

experiments.type: two-family double-curvature transfer with negative controls
experiments.limitations: Controlled manufactured fixtures with authored ground-truth edge intent. This does not infer sharp edges from arbitrary references or establish held-out asset quality.

version_scope: Typed decisions and Blender saved-state behavior verified in Blender 5.2.0 LTS.
status_note: Transferred across positive crown and negative saddle double curvature with explicit failure controls; real reference-driven use remains open.
